newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- unchanged amid low demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- unchanged amid low demand.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were mostly unchanged in quiet Friday action, as traders said demand for municipal bonds continues to sag.
"Munis are just not the hot investment product right now," one trader said. "There's not a lot of demand out there."
He said relatively low supply levels in recent months are not generating price increases because of the demand problem.
Munis ended Thursday's session down 3/8 of a point, following the 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds' nearly full-point drop.
In the government market Friday, the benchmark 30-year was up 9/32 at 99-29/32 to yield 6.63 percent.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract was off 2/32 at 117-5/32. The March T-bond contract lost 2/32 at 112-31/32. The MOB spread was unchanged from Thursday at 134 ticks.

In the muni secondary, bids on Delaware River Port Authority FGIC 5-1/2s of 2026 were up two basis points to 5.62 percent. Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5-1/4s of 2023 were up one basis point to 5.59 percent.
Next week's new deals include at least five negotiated offerings totaling $150 million or more. Morgan Stanley & Co is expected to price $490 million New York City Municipal Assistance Corp bonds.
Goldman Sachs is expected to price $260 million New York State Thruway Authority bonds, while Smith Barney Inc is set to bring a $250 million Cook County, Ill., deal.
Also next week, Smith Barney is expected to price $250 million San Diego Public Facilities Financial Authority, Calif, bonds and $150 million Platte River Power Authority, Colo., bonds.
